To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the economic crisis has had an adverse impact on young people’s lives across Europe.

1) the crisis had a strong impact on the economic situation of young people, especially in the Southern European countries, 2) the economic situation of the young people in the Eastern European countries is the most precarious, and 3) there is a strong correlation between the economic situation of youth and the level of welfare state provision in the country.

1) the economic crisis has been associated with a significant increase in poverty, unemployment and co-residence for young people; 2) these changes have not been uniform across European countries; 3) the effects of the economic crisis have been mitigated in countries with more generous welfare state provision, and 4) the economic crisis seems to have been more adverse for young people in countries with less generous welfare state provision.

how young people have fared during the economic crisis and how welfare state provisions might have buffered their vulnerability.
